subject: CureSync eval ops & scope - post-call recap and MAP
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@curesync.com>, Patricia D'Souza <patricia.dsouza@curesync.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: CureSync eval ops & scope - post-call recap and MAP

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clear description of your use case (clinical triage summarization + EHR context enrichment). Below is a concise recap, recommended next steps for an initial model-fit / quality benchmark run on Redwood, and the mutual action plan (MAP) I promised.

Recap (call notes)
- Primary goal: improve accuracy of triage-recommendation summaries while keeping mean latency < 250ms for single-pass API calls at 8k context (95th pct).
- Data: de-identified triage transcripts (CSV export + JSON context), roughly 12k candidate records for initial eval.
- Security: CureSync prefers Private deployment or dedicated tenancy; procurement requires SOC2 evidence and standard DPA.

Model suggestions (shortlist for benchmarking)
- Redwood-curated medium: 13B quantized variant (good cost/quality tradeoff for instruction-following summarization).
- Redwood-curated large: 34B int8 (higher-quality baseline for edge cases).
- Small distilled option: 7B q4f16 for low-cost fallbacks (useful for A/B latency/cost tradeoffs).

Eval plan (high level)
- Format: CSV with columns [id, prompt, reference_summary, context_bucket]. See attached curesync_eval_template_v1.csv for exact schema.
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, BLEU (where applicable), sentence-BERT cosine for semantic similarity, and a human-rated acceptability tag (0/1).
- Minimum sample: 2k records per critical workflow to reach statistical power for variance checks; we'll start with 3k to be safe.

Next steps (action items)
- CureSync: share sample export (2k de-identified records) to S3 prefix or Drive link by Oct 21. Procurement to share PO terms if going private/dedicated.
- Redwood: spin up the eval cluster, run model variants, deliver benchmarking report with scoring breakdown and recommended production model by Oct 28.
- Joint: 30-min review of results week of Nov 1 (I'll send a calendar invite once results are in).

Attachments: curesync_eval_template_v1.csv (dataset schema), MAP_CureSync_Q4.pdf (mutual action plan PDF).

Let me know if I captured anything incorrectly. If this looks good I will ask Priyom to post the detailed scoring rubric + S3 ingest instructions to the shared Drive.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful and captures the call. A couple of clarifying questions before we share the sample export: 

1) Scoring rubric: can you share the exact thresholds you consider "pass" for the initial benchmark? For instance, what semantic-similarity cutoff would you recommend for automatic acceptability vs human review?
2) Private deployment: we need to confirm whether the initial eval can run in our VPC (preferred) or whether we must send the sample to Redwood's hosted eval cluster. If in-VPC is possible, what's the minimal ops/eval footprint (GPUs, time)?
3) Procurement: Patricia is on this thread — can you confirm the earliest date you can accept a PO and whether Redwood has a standard PO template?

I'll try to get the de-identified sample uploaded by Oct 21 as discussed.

— Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Clinical ML, CureSync
alex.morgan@curesync.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@curesync.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CureSync eval ops & scope - post-call recap and MAP

Alex — quick answers and the detailed ops checklist below. I'll also drop these to the Drive folder referenced in Ben's note.

1) Scoring thresholds (suggested initial guardrails)
- Semantic (sentence-BERT cosine): >= 0.82 = automatic pass; 0.75-0.82 = flagged for human review; < 0.75 = fail.
- ROUGE-L: use as secondary; baseline target > 0.45 for acceptable summaries in aggregate.
- Human acceptability: target >= 85% pass on the 3k sample to validate for production rollout.

2) In-VPC eval capability
- Yes, we can run the eval runner in your VPC via a short-lived private agent (we'll ship a small orchestrator container and request read-only S3/GCS access or mounted Drive). Minimum footprint: 1x A10G or equivalent for 4-6 hours for a 3k sample on a 13B quantized model. For the 34B variant plan on 1x A100 for ~6-10 hours depending on batching and prefix caching. We'll provide exact cost estimates in the MAP.

3) Procurement & PO
- We accept PO; details: Redwood standard commercial terms + DPA (we can provide the template). Earliest acceptance: as soon as PO signed and SOW attached. Patricia, I'll send the PO template and SOC2 summary to procurement if you confirm.

Ops checklist for dataset ingest (copy/paste friendly)
- Required: CSV with header row. Columns: id, prompt, reference_summary, context_json (escaped), source_date, anonymization_tag.
- Encoding: UTF-8, LF line endings.
- Sample sizes: 3k primary + up to 1k for stress cases (edge workflows).
- Scoring script: we will provide a scoring runner (Python) that outputs per-id metrics and aggregate JSON (we'll host in Drive). Please do not include PHI in the sample; anonymize and mark anonymization_tag.

Link to scoring repo + rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3CureSyncEvalFolder
HubSpot record: HS-98234

I'll put a calendar placeholder for the Nov 2 review (tentative). Ben — do you want me to own the in-VPC setup once CureSync confirms the S3/agent details?

Thanks,
Priyom

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Priyom. Folks, attaching the MAP_CureSync_Q4.pdf that lays out responsibilities, timeline, and decision gates. Short MAP summary below with target dates: 

Mutual Action Plan (high level)
- Oct 21: CureSync uploads 3k de-identified sample + edge cases to agreed S3 prefix (action: Alex)
- Oct 22: Redwood confirms access and deploys eval agent in CureSync VPC (action: Priyom)
- Oct 23-25: Run benchmarks on 13B q4f16 + 34B int8 (action: Redwood infra team)
- Oct 28: Deliver scoring report (per-metric breakdown, failure modes, recommended production model) (action: Ben)
- Nov 2: Joint review call to decide pilot rollout path (action: all)

Open asks for CureSync before we start:
- Confirm S3 location + IAM read-only role (we'll provide a template inline)
- Confirm whether you want the 7B fallback included in the first run (cost-add: low)
- Procurement: is a PO expected before agent deploy or post-report? We can accommodate either but need to know for legal.

Patricia — if you can confirm the procurement flow we will queue the SOC2 & DPA docs to you immediately.

Ben
